title: Compound Assignment
description:
## The Problem
Notice that if you do something like:
```ts
let x: number = 10;
x + 5;
console.log(x); // still 10!
```
`x` doesn't change. `x + 5` calculates 15 but doesn't store it anywhere. You'd have to do `x = x + 5` to actually update it.

## The Shortcut
Writing `x = x + 5` every time is annoying. So TypeScript gives you compound assignment:
- `x += 5` is the same as `x = x + 5`
- `x -= 5` is the same as `x = x - 5`
- `x *= 5` is the same as `x = x * 5`
- `x /= 5` is the same as `x = x / 5`

## Even Shorter
Adding or subtracting 1 is so common it gets its own operator:
- `x++` is the same as `x += 1`
- `x--` is the same as `x -= 1`
